traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.62, 0.62, 0.55], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.limb_course.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 121): 'slender remote and often contorted branches somewhat pendulous toward the ends'.

traits.branch_posture.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 121): 'slender remote and often contorted branches somewhat pendulous toward the ends'.

appearance.bark_look.stages.white.note: stage: text: 'greenish or yellowish white to gray and smooth' (FNA); 'roughened by horizontal bands of circular wart-like excrescences' (Sargent); white powder (summary of Rabinowitz & Tripp 2015). Branch-scar eyes come from the mesh, not the tile; until_diameter_m: inferred (photo)

appearance.bark_look.stages.furrowed.note: stage: text: 'near the base of old trees nearly black ... deeply divided into broad flat ridges broken on the surface into small appressed plate-like scales' (Sargent); 'shallowly furrowed only basally' (FNA)

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Populus tremuloides (read 2026-10-18): the leaves "become golden to yellow, rarely red, in autumn". Colour ours.

appearance.twig.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17), as Populus tremuloides: "slender branchlets covered with scattered oblong orange-colored lenticels, bright red-brown and very lustrous during their first season, gradually turning light gray tinged with red, ultimately dark gray". Colour chosen by eye for bright red-brown.

traits.shade_tolerance.note: FEIS's quaking aspen review (Populus tremuloides, read 2026-10-16): "Quaking aspen is shade intolerant and cannot reproduce beneath its own canopy."

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Populus tremuloides: grows 30 m to 35 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Populus tremuloides: leaves 3 cm to 5 cm long.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Populus tremuloides: petioles slender, laterally flattened, about equalling the leaves (3 cm to 5 cm).

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Aspen, quaking, green: modulus of elasticity 5,900 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.35). Table 4-1 gives one row for aspen, quaking and bigtooth together.

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Aspen, quaking, green: modulus of rupture 35,000 kPa (clear wood in static bending). Table 4-1 gives one row for aspen, quaking and bigtooth together.

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1, Aspen, quaking: average moisture content of green wood, heartwood 95% and sapwood 113% of oven-dry mass; stated as a share, the range between them with its middle typical where both are given. Table 4-1 gives one row for aspen, quaking and bigtooth together.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Populus tremuloides (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.41 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 516 records in 7 sources); trunks 0.41, branches 0.44. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.pipe_tip.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B): the twig's and the leaf's pipe radii are scaled together so the stem's diameter at breast height matches the oldest reference size; the fuller crowns of broadleaf revision 11 carry more leaf, so the yearly rings (pipe_rings) are fitted near zero and the pipe model sets the diameter. Since broadleaf revision 28 its pipe_organ and pipe_rings are the broadleaf trees' rules (0, with Leonardo's rule and dead twigs kept as heartwood); this pipe_tip stays.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Howard 1996, read): quaking aspen first flowers at 2 to 3 years; large seed crops from 10 to 20. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of broadleaf's default of 4 years.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a slender, clonal tree with a narrow crown and small, round, finely toothed leaves on flattened stalks. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 15 m tall and 25 cm across at breast height at 40 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaves; smooth, chalky white bark with dark scars. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth whitish bark with dark marks and lenticels; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves somewhat smaller and narrower than shade leaves; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.leaf_apex.note: FNA, Populus tremuloides (read 2026-10-18): the blade tip is acuminate to acute.
